reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it guides viewers to buy Hedget through FTX and an auction while directing them to join through a linked URL. It solicits participation involving level-2 KYC, fund transfers, crypto payment, MetaMask wallet interaction, high bidding, short timing windows, and a claimed token benefit. The disclaimer and wallet-safety warning limit conclusions about intent or outcomes but do not remove the described solicitation mechanism.

opening.argument: Judge the profit discussion as investment commentary, not a promise of returns. The presenter explicitly leaves the buying decision to viewers and asks them to exercise diligence. The opening disclaimer also describes cryptocurrency investing as highly speculative and puts investment decisions at the viewer's own risk. Even when discussing how to participate, he warns against untrusted wallet QR codes. Those cautions matter: the video does not establish that a purchase will be profitable or that the presenter can protect anyone from loss.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the presenter explains participation, but an explanation is not itself evidence of deception. Its profit quote says viewers can take an opportunity to make a profit, not that profit is certain. The cited personal account of a previous bid likewise cannot establish what a viewer will receive this time. The explicit instruction to decide whether to buy remains important context for those statements.

citations.quote: But if you're already in business, then you can take this opportunity to make a profit

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The disclaimer limits any claim of guaranteed returns, but it does not make the presentation merely detached commentary. The presenter urges viewers to complete KYC promptly so they can invest, gives specific bidding advice, and connects participation to profit. A wallet warning does not negate that funded purchase pathway.

opening.argument: This is substantially a walkthrough of how an auction works. The presenter says he will explain participation, uses a prior Serum screenshot, and describes where the bid option appears. The sampled material also shows auction rules, including how bids above the threshold are filled and how unused collateral is returned. That procedural detail gives viewers information for assessing an unfamiliar process; showing the steps does not prove that anyone completed a purchase or received a return.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's phrase 'how you can participate' accurately identifies a tutorial, but does not resolve whether the instruction is deceptive. The cited higher-bidding statement describes the presenter's intended approach, while the on-screen auction material lays out conditional bidding and fulfillment rules. The reference to a possible resale price is not evidence of a completed resale or appreciation.

citations.quote: So now I will tell you how you can participate
So as I told you I will try higher bidding of buying

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is precisely what makes the solicitation actionable. Beyond explaining rules, the presenter tells viewers to transfer funds, recommends a highest bid to improve their chances, and gives rapid submission instructions. The auction documents do not turn those purchase directions into neutral instruction.

citations.quote: after creating all accounts, send a fund.
This will be the highest bid which will give us high chances to participate in this bid.
Within 5 to 10 seconds you have to get all the work done.

opening.argument: The evidence describes a token auction through an identified exchange, with stated bidding rules and a purchase price, rather than an unexplained payment demand. The displayed rules say a filled bid results in a trade for tokens; the presenter discusses KYC and funding as parts of participation. The description includes an exchange sign-up link, but these records do not establish a guaranteed return, a request to disclose credentials to the presenter, or a completed diversion of funds. Those missing facts should matter before treating an ordinary purchase process as a demonstrated scam.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution lists real participation steps, but KYC, funding, bidding and wallet interaction are also described in the displayed auction materials; their presence alone does not show that the presenter takes viewers' money. Its cited OTC passage offers a price comparison, not proof that tokens will resell at that price. The linked exchange invitation is promotional, but the supplied evidence does not show a guaranteed payout or a completed fraudulent transfer.

citations.quote: And now, if we talk about OTC As it is sold at 15-20 dollars Hegit is currently only at this point about 15 to 20 USD which is easy to sell.
JOIN FTX https://ftx.com/#a=1363711

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A guaranteed return or completed theft is not necessary to recognize the promotional purchase mechanism here. The presenter directs viewers to join the exchange, complete KYC, fund participation and bid high, while describing a profit opportunity and tokens as easy to sell. The defense identifies uncertainty about outcomes, but does not answer the combined effect of those directions.
